item.title: Crash Due to Traffic Queues (Temporary Lights Issue), 21st October
item.description:
Due to the hopelessness of the "temporary" lights, queing traffic blocked the view for a driver turning right from the old Volkswagen site onto runnings road (eastbound). As they emerged through the westbound queue they hit a motorcyclist travelling eastbound. Traffic flows much better when the temporary lights are not working, improving visibilty for merging traffic. Queuing traffic is also causes a pollution issue. Street lighting is also not working, possibly due to the same mains fault reported on the permanent lights. This makes it hazardous for pedestrians, especially in the longer hours of darkness. The traffic light problem needs resolving NOW before more incidents occur.

item.title: Unclear lane markings on approach to roundabout causing confusion and near misses., 21st October
item.description:
The issue is on Hatherley Lane, travelling from Arle Court Roundabout towards B&Q and the retail park, on the approach to the next roundabout. There are two lanes on the approach, but there is very little clear road marking to tell drivers which lane they should use for the different exits. This regularly causes confusion, with vehicles approaching in one lane and then attempting to change lanes or move across as they reach the roundabout. I have witnessed a number of near misses here, including situations where it has not been clear which lane a vehicle intends to follow. The current markings do not give drivers enough advance warning to position themselves correctly. Please could the lane signage and road markings at this junction be reviewed, with clear destination arrows or lane information painted on Hatherley Lane before the roundabout so drivers know which lane to use well before reaching the junction.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Hatherley Lane, Hatherley, Cheltenham, Cheltenham
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Persistent flooding across footpath making it difficult and sometimes impassable after rain., 21st October
item.description:
The issue is on the footpath opposite 166 Farmfield Road, by the barriers leading to the adjoining green space. Every time it rains, a substantial amount of water pools across this section of the path. The surface appears to be uneven or slightly sunken, preventing the water from draining away properly and leaving pedestrians with little or no dry route through. This is a well-used pedestrian route, including by dog walkers, people with pushchairs and those with limited mobility. When the water pools, users either have to walk through it and get wet feet or try to negotiate the surrounding ground. Please could the surface and drainage at this location be inspected, with suitable works carried out to prevent water continually collecting across the path.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 16, Stancombe Grove, Warden Hill, Cheltenham, Cheltenham
Report on FixMyStreet
